questions.topic: Evaluations of a correlated subquery
questions.learningObjective: Explain how a correlated subquery is evaluated
questions.stem: Describe why a correlated subquery runs once per outer row rather than once total.

answer.exemplar: A correlated subquery references columns from the outer query, so its result depends on the current outer row; the engine must re-evaluate it for each outer row because the binding changes, unlike an uncorrelated subquery which runs once.

questions.explanation: Correlation makes the inner query depend on outer row values, forcing repeated evaluation. An uncorrelated subquery has no outer reference and evaluates once.

questions.stem: Explain how to collapse duplicate links into one row per distinct entity.

answer.exemplar: Group by the entity key and keep one representative link, or use DISTINCT on the entity key, so each distinct entity contributes exactly one row.

questions.explanation: Grouping or DISTINCT collapses duplicates to one row per entity. Keeping all links leaves inflation.

questions.topic: A cost claim against the plan
questions.learningObjective: Validate a cost claim with actuals
questions.stem: A DBA claims plan X is cheaper based on estimated cost; what should you check next?

options.text: Trust the estimate and ship it
Increase the cost threshold
Disable statistics
Compare actual execution time and rows

questions.explanation: Estimated cost must be validated with actual runtime and row counts. Tuning thresholds or disabling stats misleads.

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.topic: Duplicate share of a multiplied result
questions.learningObjective: Reduce duplicate share
questions.stem: Explain how to reduce the duplicate share in a multiplied join result.

answer.exemplar: Deduplicate each input on its join key before joining, or change the join to a semi-join, so duplicate keys no longer multiply the result rows.

questions.explanation: Deduplicating inputs removes multiplication. A semi-join returns one row per left row when a match exists.

questions.topic: Reading a plan for a table scan
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish index cond from filter
questions.stem: A plan shows Seq Scan with Index Cond; what does that imply?

options.text: An index condition is applied during the scan
No index is used and all rows are read
The table is skipped entirely
The query returned no rows

questions.explanation: Index Cond means an index condition is applied while scanning. A plain Filter would mean post-read filtering.

questions.topic: Reading a plan for a table scan
questions.learningObjective: Read a scan node details
questions.stem: A plan shows Seq Scan with Filter; what does Filter indicate?

options.text: An index handled the predicate
The table is not read at all
Rows are filtered after being read
The query returned no rows

questions.explanation: The Filter is applied to rows after the scan reads them. An index condition would appear as Index Cond instead.

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.topic: An index that a query cannot use
questions.learningObjective: Avoid function on indexed column
questions.stem: Explain how to keep an index usable when filtering on a transformed value.

answer.exemplar: Store the transformed value in a generated column and index that, or rewrite the predicate to compare the raw column against a transformed literal.

questions.explanation: Indexing the transformed value or transforming the literal keeps the index usable. Transforming the column blocks it.

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.topic: A join result larger than both inputs
questions.learningObjective: Quantify join inflation
questions.stem: Left table has 4 rows with key A repeated twice; right has 3 rows with key A repeated 3 times; how many rows for key A?
questions.explanation: Two left rows times three right rows gives six. Adding gives five.

questions.topic: Reading a composite index order
questions.learningObjective: Use index for ordered output
questions.stem: Index on (a, b); query orders by a only; can the index provide order?

options.text: No, both columns must be in ORDER BY
Yes, but only if b is filtered
No, b must be sorted first
Yes, a is the leading column

questions.explanation: Ordering by the leading column alone can use the index order. The second column need not appear in ORDER BY.

questions.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
questions.topic: Reading duplicated rows across pages
questions.learningObjective: Detect offset pagination duplicates

stimulus.body: Page 1 ids: 1,2,3. Page 2 ids: 3,4,5. One id repeats.

questions.stem: How many distinct ids appear across both pages?

options.text: 5 distinct ids
4 distinct ids
6 distinct ids
3 distinct ids

questions.explanation: Six displayed slots minus one repeated id gives five distinct ids. Counting slots ignores the repeat.
